facts.subject: language
facts.text: Onomatopoeia are words that sound like what they mean, such as buzz and splash.

facts.subject: math

facts.subject: math
facts.text: Euclid's Elements was used as a maths textbook for more than 2,000 years.

facts.subject: math
facts.text: The golden ratio is about 1.618.

facts.text: Computers have worked out the digits of pi to trillions of places.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: DNA has the shape of a double helix, like a twisted ladder.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: Light travels at 299,792,458 metres per second in a vacuum.

facts.subject: science
facts.text: The human body is made of tens of trillions of cells.

facts.subject: science

facts.text: The United Nations was founded in 1945.

facts.subject: world
facts.text: More than 8 billion people live on Earth.

facts.text: Antibiotics work against bacteria, not viruses.

facts.subject: digital

facts.subject: digital
facts.text: A cookie is a small piece of data a website stores in your browser.

facts.subject: money

facts.text: Bitcoin, the first widely used cryptocurrency, was launched in 2009.

facts.subject: thinking
facts.text: Correlation does not imply causation: two things happening together does not prove one causes the other.

facts.text: The painter Frida Kahlo is famous for her many self-portraits.

facts.text: Open-source software is software whose source code anyone can read and share.
